newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone army reopens highway, kills 10 rebels.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone army reopens highway, kills 10 rebels.

text.p: Sierra Leone's army has smashed a rebel base used to launch attacks on the strategic Bo to Freetown highway, killing 10 rebels, military officials said on Thursday.

The private South African security firm Executive Outcomes provided helicopter support for Tuesday's attack and the government had set up a special task force to monitor the highway and keep in open, they added.

But officials in the north said that rebels had killed four civilians and a soldier on Thursday in an ambush of a vehicle in which they were travelling on the Makeni to Koidu Town road. The civilians were going to repair a food truck on the road.

Officials say the attack on the rebel base was not intended to compromise a truce agreed by the government and rebels during peace talks in Ivory Coast but that the army had had to act to end a two-week rebel blockade of the Bo-Freetown highway.

It was not immediately clear whether the rebels who attacked the road were acting alone or on orders from Foday Sankoh, their leader who has been in Ivory Coast since the April peace talks with President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah's newly elected government.
The blockade of the Bo-Freetown highway had been hitting supplies to the capital, the officials said.

Sankoh launched the war, which has killed an estimated 10,000 people, in 1991. The peace talks have stalled on rebel demands for the withdrawal of all foreign forces -- Nigerian and Guinean troops plus Executive Outcomes.
